investigation: Relativistic Pseudospin Symmetry (PSS) and Spin-Orbit Splitting across Mass Regions
description: Systematic evaluation of pseudospin doublets across valley-of-stability benchmarks (208Pb, 132Sn, 48Ca) to neutron drip-line nuclei (24O, 70Ca), demonstrating the breakdown of PSS driven by diffuse surface halo expansion and pseudo-centrifugal decoupling.

boundary_1_diffuseness_driven_pss_breakd.mechanism: In stable heavy nuclei, Ginocchio's condition d(V+S)/dr = 0 is approximately satisfied in the interior, and its surface peak is narrow enough that the radial wave function nodes of the doublet cancel the overlap integral, keeping Delta E_PSS < 0.35-0.50 MeV. At the neutron drip line, weak binding creates an extended halo/skin with diffuseness a > 0.88 fm. The broad surface slope overlaps with the entire asymptotic tail of the wave function, destroying node cancellation and causing PSS splitting to surge by 5 to 10-fold (reaching 3.61 MeV in 24O).
boundary_1_diffuseness_driven_pss_breakd.failure_signature: Severe underestimation of single-particle gaps and false assumption of doublet degeneracy when applying stable-nucleus RMF parameterizations to drip-line systems.

boundary_2_pseudo_spin_orbit_inversion.contrast: Normal ordering (E(j_<) > E(j_>)) vs Inverted ordering
boundary_2_pseudo_spin_orbit_inversion.mechanism: While in deeply bound states the j_< = l_tilde - 1/2 state is systematically slightly above j_> = l_tilde + 1/2, near the drip line the centrifugal barrier for the l_tilde component decouples from the s-wave/p-wave continuum, inverting the doublet order (as observed in 70Ca where 2d3/2 drops below 3s1/2).
boundary_2_pseudo_spin_orbit_inversion.failure_signature: Inversion of spin-parity assignments of low-lying states in drip-line nuclei.
